question: does dropping motor hold on NEW subjects, or was 0.7369 a fold-selected value?
how: train on 728, predict 233 never-seen subjects, with motor and without, on the two extractions that exist outside the 753 (our own 400 and the 450 re-extraction). The published Ooi features cannot be used here.
verdict: MOTOR DROP DOES NOT REPRODUCE OUT OF SAMPLE. Both extractions lose slightly from removing motor (-0.0019 and -0.0021), though neither interval excludes zero. So the in-fold +0.0034 is inside the out-of-sample noise, and the honest status of 'drop motor' is: it costs nothing and may help in-fold, but it has not been shown to help on new subjects.
consistent_with_what: this is the same shape as everything else in this project: a +0.002-0.003 in-fold gain that the 233-subject test cannot resolve. The difference from the other levers is that here the out-of-sample point estimate is negative, not merely zero.
consequence_for_the_canonical: DROP_MOTOR=True is defensible as a DEFAULT (it removes a run; nothing in the data says the run matters) but the paper must not claim it improves generalisation. Say: the motor run contributes nothing measurable, the default no longer uses it, in-fold 0.7369, and on 233 new subjects 0.7466 vs 0.7485 (difference inside noise).

parallel_session_diagnostic_supported_ou.their D1 in-fold-selected 0.7291 approx: yes, the selector reaches language x2
